did_you_know.text: Did you know? The chapter places Hosea’s prophecy during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and during the reign of Jeroboam son of Jehoash, king of Israel.
Did you know? Hosea’s first mission is presented through a symbolic action: the LORD commands him to take a wife and have children to illustrate the people’s abandonment of the LORD.
Did you know? Hosea obeys the command and marries Gomer daughter of Diblaim; the birth of the first son begins a series of children’s names with prophetic significance.
Did you know? The name of the first son, Jezreel, is connected to the LORD’s declaration that he will punish the house of Jehu for the bloodshed at Jezreel and bring an end to the kingdom of Israel.
Did you know? The Valley of Jezreel also appears as a symbol of military defeat: the LORD says that there he will break Israel’s bow.

Did you know? The daughter is named Lo-Ruhamah, and her name expresses the LORD’s declaration that he will no longer show mercy to the house of Israel, while the following verse says that the house of Judah will receive mercy.
Did you know? According to the chapter, Judah’s deliverance will not come through bow, sword, war, horses, or horsemen, but through the LORD their God.
Did you know? The name of the third son, Lo-Ammi, expresses the breakdown of the relationship: “You are not my people, and I am not your God.”

Did you know? The chapter distinguishes between the house of Israel and the house of Judah: Israel is given names and symbols of judgment and separation, while Judah is promised mercy and deliverance.
